warnings.warning: County-centre coordinates are not representative for unusually shaped counties.
County area and FIPS/geography provenance are external inputs not frozen in the paper.
Reports-per-area is only a proxy for drug-use density and can reflect policing/reporting intensity.
The gravity analogy is not a causal mechanism for human drug spread.
Inverse-square distance is selected without comparing exponential or network alternatives.
The Haversine formula's radians, Earth radius, and coordinate units are not fully audited.
External influence sums over the selected counties and omits out-of-sample neighboring states.
The assumption that rural populations are more susceptible to outside influence is untested.
The assumption that no new drug appears through 2025 conflicts with the paper's epidemic-wave background.
The assumption that addiction continues its current trend without external influence is strong and unvalidated.
Quadratic weighting `(year-2009)^2` needs sign/orientation and normalization clarification.
Recent-year emphasis can overreact to reporting shocks or one-off outbreaks.
The trend derivative requires at least two years of reports, leaving sparse counties weakly represented.
The normalization ratio median/current influence can be unstable near zero or extreme values.
The spread update adds external influence and trend without a calibrated time or count scale.
The MATLAB iteration is implementation evidence, not independently executed verification.
Drug-specific extensions face low counts and too few reporting counties.
